# Day-wise view of the 24 h-ahead forecasts (generated by `scripts/run_daywise.py`; plan task 9.8)

Git commit `a0d263587a`. Declared in `docs/experiment_protocol.md` (entry of 2026-10-19) before any number was computed. No model was fitted or re-run: the hourly 24 h-ahead test predictions saved by the single test run were aggregated. Test days 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-24: 355 days with all 24 valid hours (of 359 days with any valid hour; days with a missing hour are excluded). Each hour of a day is the 24 h-ahead forecast issued exactly 24 h earlier, so a day's 24 forecasts come from 24 different issue times (a stitched rolling day-ahead, not one forecast issued once per day); this is optimistic compared with an operational day-ahead forecast. Daily energy = sum of the 24 hourly values / 1000 (MU; the hourly series is a snapshot at the start of each hour, so this approximates energy). Daily peak = maximum hourly value; peak hour = clock hour of the maximum. Intervals: 95% paired moving-block bootstrap over whole days (block 28 days, 1,000 resamples, fixed seed).

## Reference: the Zenodo daily study (units only)

`reports/daily_multiyear.md` forecasts the daily total directly from daily data (Zenodo series, a different dataset and different periods). Its 1-day-ahead MAE in MU: 2024 fold (1 January to 28 April 2024) naive 116.1, ridge 51.1, XGBoost 45.6, LSTM 48.6; mean of the five clean folds naive 132.4, ridge 48.8, XGBoost 48.8, LSTM 49.7. The numbers above are not a like-for-like comparison with these (different period, different data, hourly-derived energy), only the same unit.

## Caveats

- One test year, so about 355 daily errors; the intervals reflect day-to-day sampling noise within that year, not year-to-year variation.
- The 24 forecasts of a day are not issued at one time; a real day-ahead forecast issued once (for example at 10:00 on the previous day) must look 14-37 h ahead and would be less accurate. That is the parked task 9.7.
- Daily energy from hourly snapshots is an approximation of the metered energy.
- Peak hour is defined as the hour of the maximum; when the evening and the morning peaks are close in size the exact hour is unstable, so the within-1-hour share is the more informative number.
- The test year has been used several times for declared analyses; this view only re-aggregates predictions already produced and tunes nothing.
